name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs—open and merged—for two weeks. This catches unsafe changes before they merge while giving full coverage of edge cases. The trade-off is higher compute cost, but it’s safer than limiting to merged PRs where damage is already done.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode trains reviewers to dismiss *all* autofeedback as noise, not just false positives—PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs risks training reviewers to ignore *all* automated signals, not just the unsafe ones. A better alternative is running it only on high-risk PRs (e.g., dependency updates, config changes) where the cost of oversight outweighs the noise risk. Settle it with a controlled test: measure reviewer response rates to autofeedback in shadow mode vs. no shadow mode for 2 weeks.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode only on open PRs flagged as high-risk by a lightweight risk classifier (e.g., dependency updates, major refactors) for one week, then switch to me; this cuts compute cost by 70% while still catching unsafe changes early.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on open PRs flagged high-risk by a lightweight classifier for one week, then switch to me. This catches unsafe changes early without wasting compute on low-risk PRs. The trade-off is missing edge cases in low-risk PRs, but those are less likely to cause damage.
